name: West Virginia
overview: West Virginia provides separate refundable senior, excess-property-tax and disabled-veteran credits, with rules preventing duplicate relief.

programs.name: Senior Citizens Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: Homestead Exemption participant: 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled.
programs.incomeDefinition: Current payment-year federal adjusted gross income; the poverty threshold uses the statutory family unit residing in the homestead, not automatically the federal tax-unit count.
programs.incomeLimits: 150% federal poverty guidelines: $23,475 for one person in 2025, plus $8,250 for each additional person.
programs.maximumBenefit: Eligible taxes on the next $20,000 taxable assessed value above the homestead exemption.
programs.formulaSummary: Refunds qualifying Class II tax paid on that assessed-value slice.
programs.application: Use original SCTC-A from Tax Division, separately for eligible nonfilers or with IT-140.
eligibilityNotes: Must owe and pay qualifying homestead tax.
Actual entitlement to the homestead exemption is required; assessed value alone does not establish participation.
Federal alternative minimum tax liability disqualifies the claimant. The statutory restriction differs from the overview webpage’s AMT wording.
A calculated credit below $10 is subject to a statutory refund restriction; this does not by itself establish that every offset against income tax is zero.
interactions: Reduces HEPTC; cannot combine with Disabled Veteran Property Tax Credit.
programs.programYear: 2025 income and qualifying tax payments during 2025; underlying property-tax assessment years may differ.

programs.name: Homestead Excess Property Tax Credit
programs.incomeDefinition: 2025 federal AGI plus statutory additions, tax-exempt interest, workers’ compensation/loss-of-earnings insurance and nontaxable Social Security for the burden calculation. Separately filed household members’ income requires reconciliation.
programs.incomeLimits: Program low-income test based on 300% federal poverty guidelines.
programs.formulaSummary: Eligible owner-occupied real-property taxes, after senior credit, exceeding 4% of gross household income, capped at $1,000.
programs.application: File HEPTC-1 with IT-140 and property-tax receipt.
eligibilityNotes: Homestead Exemption participation is not required.
Every whole or partial owner must satisfy the low-income test; the claimant’s own income alone is insufficient.
Federal alternative minimum tax liability disqualifies the claimant.
The statute and dedicated 2025 form use 2025 income and payments. The overview webpage’s 2024-income sentence is inconsistent.
interactions: Calculate senior credit first; subtract it.
Cannot combine with Disabled Veteran Property Tax Credit.
programs.programYear: 2025 income and qualifying property-tax payments during 2025.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Real Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: Honorably discharged veteran with qualifying service-connected disability; qualifying unremarried surviving spouse.
programs.maximumBenefit: Eligible homestead real-property taxes timely paid during the income-tax year.
programs.formulaSummary: Refundable credit for qualifying homestead taxes, limited by statutory veteran criteria and timely payment.
programs.application: File DV-1 with property-tax receipts and VA disability-rating letter.
eligibilityNotes: 2025 law requires an honorably discharged veteran with at least 90% permanent and total disability solely due to service-connected disabilities.
The July 11, 2025 amendment adds qualifying unmarried surviving spouses of veterans who previously received this credit. Midyear payment and termination treatment remains unresolved.
interactions: Alternative to Senior Citizens Tax Credit and HEPTC.
programs.programYear: Qualifying timely payments during income-tax year 2025, including specified payments on underlying 2024 and 2025 property-tax bills.

programs.name: Homestead Exemption
programs.ageRule: 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled.
programs.formulaSummary: Assessed-value exemption administered by county assessor; it precedes senior-credit calculations.

laterChanges: Current veteran definitions include later 2026 changes, including individual-unemployability wording. Those changes are not evidence of 2025 entitlement.
researchNotes: The statute controls the 2025 income year and AMT disqualification where the overview conflicts. Partial payments, mixed assessment cohorts, legal family membership and some household-income attribution require additional facts.

The existing senior-credit formula at the audited canonical commit uses assessed value as a dollar credit. Its source mapping is now identified, but that formula is not validated. A separate model correction is in progress.
Compute SCTC before HEPTC. Disabled-veteran relief excludes both. Sub-$10 refund settlement and any combined-cap interpretation remain explicit calculation gaps.
